issues.description: The database instance is typed as 'any', completely bypassing TypeScript's type safety. This creates an exploitable vulnerability where any method can be called on the db object without validation, potentially allowing SQL injection if the underlying library's API is misused.
issues.suggestion: Create a proper type definition for NeverChangeDB or import its type from the library. Example: 'let db: NeverChangeDB | null = null;' This ensures type-safe usage throughout the codebase and prevents accidental misuse of the database API.

issues.description: No validation or sanitization of user input before database operations. The 'text' parameter in addTodo and updateTodo accepts any string without length limits or content validation. While parameterized queries prevent SQL injection, missing validation enables denial-of-service attacks (unbounded data storage) and data integrity issues (empty/malicious content).
issues.suggestion: Add input validation at the function entry point. Example: if (!text || text.trim().length === 0) throw new Error('Todo text cannot be empty'); if (text.length > 1000) throw new Error('Todo text exceeds maximum length');

issues.description: Critical logic bug in initDb function. Line 7 contains 'if(db) db;' which is a no-op statement. This appears to be an incomplete early-return check, meaning initDb will reinitialize the database and re-run migrations every time it's called, potentially causing data corruption or performance issues.
issues.suggestion: Fix the early return to prevent redundant initialization. Example: 'if (db) return;' or 'if (db) return db;' depending on the intended API.

issues.description: Missing null/undefined checks for the 'db' instance. If any function (getTodos, toggleTodo, updateTodo, deleteTodo, addTodo) is called before initDb(), the code will throw a runtime error when trying to access methods on null. This is an availability vulnerability that can crash the application.
issues.suggestion: Add defensive checks in each function. Example: if (!db) throw new Error('Database not initialized. Call initDb() first.'); Alternatively, ensure initDb is called during module initialization and make db non-nullable after init.

issues.description: Migration logic uses 'any' type for the db parameter, preventing type checking. Additionally, migrations are added every time initDb() is called (due to the bug on line 7), causing unnecessary re-registration of migrations on each call.
issues.suggestion: Fix the initDb early return (line 7) to prevent re-registration. Type the migration parameter properly to match NeverChangeDB's expected type signature.

issues.description: Inconsistent error handling across functions. addTodo catches errors and logs them without re-throwing, silently swallowing failures. In contrast, updateTodo and deleteTodo catch, log, AND re-throw. toggleTodo and getTodos have no error handling at all. This inconsistency makes debugging difficult and creates unpredictable behavior.
issues.suggestion: Standardize error handling across all database functions. Either let errors propagate naturally for the caller to handle, or consistently wrap all functions with try-catch. Recommended: let errors propagate and handle at the call site.

issues.description: Console.log statements used for application logging. In production code, console.log is not appropriate for logging database operations as it cannot be configured, filtered, or redirected. These logs will clutter console output and provide no structured logging capability.
issues.suggestion: Replace console.log with a proper logging library (e.g., winston, pino) or at minimum create a logging abstraction. Example: import logger from './logger'; logger.info('Todo added successfully', { todoText: text });

issues.description: Using @ts-ignore to suppress TypeScript errors for the NeverChangeDB import. This is a code smell that indicates missing type definitions and defeats the purpose of using TypeScript. The suppressed error could be hiding important type mismatches.
issues.suggestion: Either install proper type definitions for the library, create a declaration file (e.g., neverchange.d.ts), or use a properly typed alternative. Create a minimal .d.ts file if the library has no types.

issues.description: getTodos returns 'rows || []' which suggests the query might return null/undefined. However, this fallback is unclear - if the database query fails, it should throw an error rather than silently returning an empty array, which could mask actual failures.
issues.suggestion: Make the return type explicit and handle the null case explicitly: export async function getTodos(): Promise<Todo[]> { const rows = await db.query(...); if (!rows) return []; return rows as Todo[]; }

issues.description: toggleTodo function has no error handling and no feedback mechanism. If the update fails, the caller has no way to know. This is especially problematic for UI operations where the user expects feedback.
issues.suggestion: Add proper error handling consistent with other functions, or document that errors will propagate to the caller.

codeQuality.summary: The src/db.ts file has critical security and maintainability issues that require immediate attention. Most critical: (1) A logic bug on line 7 prevents proper initialization guard, causing migrations to re-run on every call. (2) Pervasive use of 'any' type undermines TypeScript's safety guarantees. (3) Missing null checks on the db instance will cause runtime crashes if functions are called before initialization. (4) No input validation enables DoS attacks and data integrity issues. (5) Inconsistent error handling makes debugging difficult. The file needs significant refactoring to: add proper TypeScript types, fix the initialization logic, implement input validation, standardize error handling, and remove @ts-ignore suppressions. The use of parameterized queries is good and prevents SQL injection, which is the primary positive aspect of this code.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Database initialization and migration logic has zero test coverage, risking schema corruption in production. The early return logic 'if(db) db;' appears to be a bug (should be 'return db;') and needs testing to verify idempotent initialization behavior.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: should return existing db instance without reinitializing when db is already initialized. Assertion: expect(await initDb()).toBe(db) and verify db.init() was not called a second time using a spy.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Database schema initialization is critical infrastructure code. Incorrect schema means the entire application fails. Must verify all columns (id, text, completed) are created with correct types and constraints.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: should successfully create todos table with correct schema when migration version 1 runs. Assertion: await initDb(); const result = await db.query('PRAGMA table_info(todos)'); expect(result).toContainEqual(expect.objectContaining({name: 'id', type: 'INTEGER'}));

untestedPaths.reasoning: Schema migrations are critical for data integrity during upgrades. If the deleted column is not added correctly, soft-delete functionality will break and cause data loss or runtime errors.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: should add deleted column to existing todos table when migration version 2 runs. Assertion: await initDb(); const result = await db.query('PRAGMA table_info(todos)'); expect(result).toContainEqual(expect.objectContaining({name: 'deleted', type: 'BOOLEAN', dflt_value: '0'}));

untestedPaths.reasoning: Database initialization failure should propagate errors to the caller so the application can handle startup failures gracefully (retry, alert, fail-fast). Silent failures cause unpredictable behavior.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: should throw error when db.init() fails due to invalid database state. Assertion: Mock db.init() to throw new Error('Init failed'); await expect(initDb()).rejects.toThrow('Init failed');

untestedPaths.reasoning: This is the primary user-facing operation. Must verify the SQL query is correct, parameters are properly bound to prevent SQL injection, and success feedback is provided.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: should insert todo with provided text and log success message. Assertion: const consoleSpy = jest.spyOn(console, 'log'); await addTodo('Buy milk'); expect(db.execute).toHaveBeenCalledWith('INSERT INTO todos (text) VALUES (?)', ['Buy milk']); expect(consoleSpy).toHaveBeenCalledWith('Todo added successfully');

untestedPaths.reasoning: Error swallowing without throwing means callers cannot detect failures. This causes silent data loss where users think todos are saved but they're not. Critical for data integrity and user trust.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: should catch and log error when database insert fails without throwing. Assertion: const consoleErrorSpy = jest.spyOn(console, 'error'); db.execute.mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error('DB constraint violation')); await addTodo('Test'); expect(consoleErrorSpy).toHaveBeenCalledWith('Failed to add todo:', expect.any(Error));

untestedPaths.reasoning: Edge case validation: empty strings may violate business logic (todos should have content) but the code has no validation. Test documents current behavior for future validation requirements.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: should handle empty string todo text by attempting to insert it. Assertion: await addTodo(''); expect(db.execute).toHaveBeenCalledWith('INSERT INTO todos (text) VALUES (?)', ['']);

untestedPaths.reasoning: Primary read operation displaying todos to users. Must verify filtering logic (deleted = 0) works correctly and sorting shows newest first. Incorrect query returns wrong data to UI.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: should return all non-deleted todos ordered by id descending. Assertion: db.query.mockResolvedValueOnce([{id: 3, text: 'Latest', completed: 0, deleted: 0}, {id: 1, text: 'Oldest', completed: 1, deleted: 0}]); const result = await getTodos(); expect(result).toHaveLength(2); expect(result[0].id).toBe(3);

untestedPaths.reasoning: The fallback 'return rows || []' handles null/undefined from the database. This defensive code prevents crashes when db.query returns unexpected values, ensuring UI always gets an array.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: should return empty array when database returns null or undefined. Assertion: db.query.mockResolvedValueOnce(null); expect(await getTodos()).toEqual([]);

untestedPaths.reasoning: Soft-delete functionality must work correctly. If deleted todos appear in the list, it confuses users and violates the application's delete contract. Verifies WHERE clause filtering.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: should exclude todos marked as deleted from the results. Assertion: db.query.mockResolvedValueOnce([{id: 1, text: 'Active', deleted: 0}]); const result = await getTodos(); expect(result).toHaveLength(1); expect(result[0].text).toBe('Active');

untestedPaths.reasoning: Core user interaction for marking todos complete/incomplete. SQL uses NOT operator which must be verified. Incorrect id binding could toggle wrong todo. No error handling means failures are silent.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: should toggle completed status from false to true for the specified todo id. Assertion: await toggleTodo(5); expect(db.execute).toHaveBeenCalledWith('UPDATE todos SET completed = NOT completed WHERE id = ?', [5]);

untestedPaths.reasoning: No try-catch means errors propagate to caller. This behavior must be tested since callers expect exceptions. If behavior changes to swallow errors (like addTodo), existing code will break.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: should propagate error when toggle fails due to database error. Assertion: db.execute.mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error('Database locked')); await expect(toggleTodo(1)).rejects.toThrow('Database locked');

untestedPaths.reasoning: SQL UPDATE with no matching rows is not an error and succeeds silently. Test documents this behavior for edge case handling. Callers should check affected row count if validation is needed.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: should execute update statement even when todo id does not exist. Assertion: await toggleTodo(99999); expect(db.execute).toHaveBeenCalledWith('UPDATE todos SET completed = NOT completed WHERE id = ?', [99999]);

untestedPaths.reasoning: Allows users to edit todo content. Must verify parameter order in SQL (text before id) to prevent swapping values. Success logging confirms operation completed.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: should update todo text for specified id and log success message. Assertion: const consoleSpy = jest.spyOn(console, 'log'); await updateTodo(3, 'Updated text'); expect(db.execute).toHaveBeenCalledWith('UPDATE todos SET text = ? WHERE id = ?', ['Updated text', 3]);

untestedPaths.reasoning: Unlike addTodo, updateTodo logs AND rethrows errors. This is correct error handling for operations where callers need to know about failures. Test ensures error isn't swallowed and propagates properly.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: should catch database error, log it, and rethrow the error. Assertion: const consoleErrorSpy = jest.spyOn(console, 'error'); const dbError = new Error('Constraint violation'); db.execute.mockRejectedValueOnce(dbError); await expect(updateTodo(1, 'New text')).rejects.toThrow('Constraint violation');

untestedPaths.reasoning: Edge case: empty text may violate business rules but code has no validation. Test documents current permissive behavior for future validation requirements.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: should allow updating todo text to empty string. Assertion: await updateTodo(2, ''); expect(db.execute).toHaveBeenCalledWith('UPDATE todos SET text = ? WHERE id = ?', ['', 2]);

untestedPaths.reasoning: Implements soft-delete pattern to preserve data history. Must verify it updates the deleted flag rather than actual DELETE. Critical for data retention and potential undo functionality.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: should soft-delete todo by setting deleted flag to 1 and log success. Assertion: const consoleSpy = jest.spyOn(console, 'log'); await deleteTodo(7); expect(db.execute).toHaveBeenCalledWith('UPDATE todos SET deleted = 1 WHERE id = ?', [7]);

untestedPaths.reasoning: Consistent error handling with updateTodo: logs and rethrows. Critical for user feedback - if delete fails silently, users see todo still exists and lose trust in application.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: should catch database error, log it, and rethrow when delete fails. Assertion: const consoleErrorSpy = jest.spyOn(console, 'error'); const dbError = new Error('Database connection lost'); db.execute.mockRejectedValueOnce(dbError); await expect(deleteTodo(5)).rejects.toThrow('Database connection lost');

untestedPaths.reasoning: Like toggleTodo, UPDATE with no matching rows succeeds silently. Documents behavior for idempotent delete operations where deleting non-existent todo is not an error.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test: should execute soft-delete even when todo id does not exist. Assertion: await deleteTodo(99999); expect(db.execute).toHaveBeenCalledWith('UPDATE todos SET deleted = 1 WHERE id = ?', [99999]);

testCoverage.summary: ESTIMATED COVERAGE: 0% - No test file exists for src/db.ts. All 6 exported functions (initDb, addTodo, getTodos, toggleTodo, updateTodo, deleteTodo) are completely untested. CRITICAL GAPS: (1) Database initialization and migration logic has zero test coverage, risking schema corruption in production. (2) Inconsistent error handling: addTodo swallows errors (logs but doesn't throw), while updateTodo and deleteTodo rethrow - this inconsistency is untested and will cause unexpected behavior. (3) Potential bug in initDb line 7: 'if(db) db;' should likely be 'if(db) return db;' - the early return is broken. (4) No validation testing for empty strings, null values, or negative IDs. (5) Soft-delete implementation completely untested - if the deleted column filter breaks, users see deleted todos. RISK LEVEL: HIGH - This is a data access layer with no tests, handling user data persistence. Bugs here cause data loss, corruption, or silent failures.

suggestions.description: Dead code: 'if(db) db;' performs no operation. This appears to be an incomplete early-return guard that causes the database to reinitialize on every call.
suggestions.benefits: Fixes the logic to actually return early when db is already initialized, preventing redundant re-initialization and migration re-registration.

suggestions.description: Replace 'any' types with proper typing. The module uses 'any' throughout, losing TypeScript's type safety benefits and enabling potential runtime errors.
suggestions.benefits: Adds proper type safety, enables IDE autocomplete, catches potential errors at compile time rather than runtime, and removes @ts-ignore suppression.

suggestions.location: entire file (add new function, update all usages)
suggestions.description: Apply Singleton pattern with lazy initialization guard. Currently db is module-level mutable state without proper initialization checks in query methods, causing runtime errors if functions are called before initDb().
suggestions.benefits: Prevents runtime errors from calling db methods before initialization. Centralizes the null-check logic and provides clear error messages to developers.

suggestions.description: Extract migration definitions into a separate constant. Migrations array clutters the initDb function and makes it harder to maintain migration history.
suggestions.benefits: Separates data (migrations) from logic (initialization), making initDb easier to read and migrations easier to maintain, test, and version.

suggestions.description: Inconsistent error handling: addTodo catches and logs errors without re-throwing, while updateTodo and deleteTodo log and re-throw. toggleTodo has no error handling at all. Standardize the approach.
suggestions.benefits: Consistent error handling allows callers to react to failures (show error messages, retry, etc.). Swallowing errors silently makes debugging harder and creates silent data loss scenarios.

suggestions.description: toggleTodo lacks try-catch error handling but other mutating operations have it. Also has inconsistent array parameter formatting.
suggestions.benefits: Consistent error handling and formatting across all database operations improves maintainability, debugging, and user experience.

suggestions.description: Use nullish coalescing operator (??) instead of logical OR (||) for default empty array return value.
suggestions.benefits: The ?? operator is more precise than ||, only defaulting on null/undefined rather than any falsy value (like 0, '', or false). This prevents subtle bugs.

suggestions.description: Consider wrapping database operations in a class to encapsulate state and provide better structure. Current module-level state makes testing and dependency management harder.
suggestions.benefits: Encapsulates database state, makes dependencies explicit, easier to test with dependency injection, follows OOP best practices, and enables multiple database instances if needed.
